尼揚加尼揚加屬撥奏體鳴器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 122.1。演: The nyonganyonga is a plucked idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 122.1. To play it you hold the instrument with both hands so that the board sits steady in your palms, and pluck the metal tongues with thumb or index finger. A common layout puts the lowest note in the centre with the higher notes to either side, so that the thumb can reach them as it turns. A beginner can start with single plucked notes and then keep a rhythm with a division of labour between the hands; the source gives no particular tutor.
尼揚加尼揚加屬簧片琴（lamellophone）家族，發聲分類為體鳴，編號122: The nyonganyonga belongs to the lamellophone family; it is classed as an idiophone, number 122.1. The source records that instruments of this kind are mainly of wooden boards fitted with interleaved metal tongues; early tongues were of bamboo and later developed into metal keys. Some instruments often carry resonators, but the materials of the resonator and of other parts are not stated.
尼揚加尼揚加屬體鳴樂器中的彈片琴，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 122: The nyonganyonga is a lamellophone among idiophones, Hornbostel–Sachs 122.1, traditional to the Shona of Zimbabwe, with several forms developed in eastern and southern Africa. Early tongues were bamboo and later metal; wooden and bamboo tongues appeared in West Africa about three thousand years ago, metal tongues in the Zambezi valley about thirteen hundred years ago, and from there they spread across the continent. In the mid twentieth century Hugh Tracey brought out the kalimba on the model of the mbira nyunga nyunga, which made it popular outside Africa; in 2020 the craft of making and playing it was inscribed on the UNESCO list of intangible cultural heritage.
尼揚加尼揚加屬體鳴樂器中的撥奏體鳴器，傳統上用於紹納人的宗教儀式、婚禮與社交聚會: The nyonganyonga is a plucked idiophone among idiophones, used traditionally in Shona religious rites, weddings and social gatherings, often in percussion ensembles with the hosho rattles. On the modern stage it can be combined with electric guitar, bass, drum kit and brass, the modern rock instruments, drawing on traditional repertoire. Other players have carried kalimba and marimba music to the American Pacific Northwest, so a demonstration can present both traditional African ensembles and modern international line-ups.
尼揚加尼揚加為非洲體鳴樂器，屬簧片琴家族，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號: The nyonganyonga is an African idiophone of the lamellophone family, Hornbostel–Sachs 122.1. It is built as a wooden board fitted with metal tongues; the player holds it with both hands and plucks the tongues with thumb and index finger. The Shona of Zimbabwe often use it at religious rites, weddings and social gatherings, and the kalimba developed from lamellophones of this kind.
尼揚加尼揚加發出的音色明亮清脆，具有獨特的金屬質感與穿透力。這件樂器音域位於中高: The nyonganyonga has a bright, clear timbre with a distinctive metallic quality and carrying power. Its range lies in the middle and upper register, and when struck it produces a clear, springy sound. Because it is an idiophone, the sound travels straight from the body of the instrument without a resonator to amplify it, so the timbre is comparatively simple and pure. Resonance comes mainly from the vibration of the instrument's own material, which leaves a modest decay. Compared with drums its timbre is sharper, and compared with the xylophone it is similarly bright but more metallic in quality. These sound characteristics give it a prominent rhythmic marking role in traditional music, and it cuts through the sound of other instruments.
